messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 62-year-old female presents to her primary care provider complaining of a mass near her right jaw. She reports that the mass is painless and has grown very slowly over the past six months. She initially did not see a physician due to being very busy at her work as a lawyer. However, she reports that she noticed some right-sided facial weakness in the past week which prompted her to visit the physician. Her past medical history is notable for Hodgkins lymphoma as a child which required radiation therapy to the neck. She has a 20 pack-year smoking history and drinks alcohol socially. Her temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 120/85 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, and respirations are 18/min. Physical examination reveals a painless firm mass at the angle of the right jaw. There is also a small palpable firm mass beneath the floor of the mouth. A right facial droop along with an inability to elevate her right eyebrow is noted. A biopsy of one of this lesion would most likely reveal which of the following?

Options:
A. Cystic configurations of anaplastic squamous and mucoid cells
B. Non-infiltrative clusters of epithelial and mesenchymal cells
C. Epithelial cells with dense lymphoid stroma and germinal centers
D. Large basophilic binucleate cells
E. Uniform spindle cells with scant cytoplasm and cigar-shaped nuclei

Correct answer: A. Cystic configurations of anaplastic squamous and mucoid cells

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This is a head and neck pathology/oncology question about parotid mucoepidermoid carcinoma; psychiatric terms are incidental and DSM-5 content is irrelevant."}
